input.prompt: Use the reference image only as the style anchor: match its exact palette, freehand kalam linework, dense dotted fill patterns, visible cotton weave and especially its lotus-and-vine scroll border running around all four edges between two thin dotted bands. Paint a NEW scene as an authentic Srikalahasti kalamkari hand-painted textile panel, photographed flat and straight-on so the cloth fills the entire frame edge to edge. The ground of the panel is dyed deep indigo blue for night. Subject: a night scene divided into two halves by a slender flowering Tree of Life standing in the exact centre, rising from a small dotted mound, its trunk patterned with cross-hatching and scales like the reference. LEFT HALF: one young Telugu woman with long black hair in a braid, wearing a simple saree with a patterned border, seated sideways on a wooden balcony swing (oonjal) hung by two chains, holding a small plain dark mobile phone to her ear with one hand, her other hand resting in her lap, smiling softly; a small striped cat curls asleep on the swing beside her; a carved balcony railing below her. RIGHT HALF: one young man with short black hair, a neat short beard and round spectacles, wearing a plain kurta, seated on a stool at a simple wooden desk beside an open arched window with a patterned frame, holding a small plain dark mobile phone to his ear with one hand, his other hand resting on the desk beside a closed book. Both figures drawn in the classical kalamkari manner: side or three-quarter profile, large almond eyes, stylised hands with five fingers, flat patterned drapery. Each faces inward toward the central tree. One single flowing vine of lotus buds, small leaves and curling tendrils leaves her phone, loops gracefully up into the central tree, winds through its branches, and descends to his phone, joining the two of them. Above the tree: a crescent moon in ecru and turmeric yellow and scattered small eight-petalled stars in ecru and yellow across the indigo sky. Style: freehand kalam (bamboo pen) outlines in iron-black with confident, slightly irregular line weight; flat natural vegetable-dye fills only: deep madder red (brick red), indigo blue, myrobalan-turmeric yellow, green made from indigo over yellow, and undyed ecru cotton; dense hand-drawn fill patterns of dots, cross-hatching, scales and tiny petals; visible hand-woven cotton weave and slight dye bleed at the edges of colour areas. The border is madder red with ecru lotus-and-vine scroll exactly as in the reference. Exactly two people in the whole panel. Completely flat, no perspective, no shading, no gradients, no metallic gold, no 3D, no photorealism. No text, no letters, no writing, no numbers, nothing on the phone screens. No lamps, no desk lamp, no diyas, no candles, no lanterns, no fire, no flames.
